newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian brewery doubles '96 net, sees more growth.
newsitem.headline: Croatian brewery doubles '96 net, sees more growth.

text.p: Croatia's brewery Karlovacka Pivovara, in which Chilean CCU has a majority stake, almost doubled its 1996 net profit and sees a further rise this year, Vecernji List daily reported on Wednesday.
The brewery posted 41.2 million kuna net profit in 1996, compared to 23.1 million the year before.
It will pay out 10.88 million kuna in dividends and retain 26.8 million kuna, the daily said without specifying how it would be used.
It said the brewery hopes to make a net profit of 48 million kuna in 1997, in line with a foreseen rise in beer production from 1,099 million hectolitres in 1996 to 1,659 million this year.
The income from basic activity rose 9.1 million kuna to 345.9 million.

The Chile-based Compania Cervecarias Unidas, whose stake in Karlovacka Pivovara is 66.99 percent, recently said it was considering new investments in Croatia this year. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
